Flex feel (Backcountry Magazine): "One of the softest splits we've ever given Editors' Choice honors to" [35] DISAGREEMENT: Flex rating / feel. The merchant lists flex as 4.5/10 ("mid-flex") and the Backcountry Magazine editors describe it as one of their softest Editors' Choice splits. The Inertia review also describes it as having a "forgiving flex." These suggest the board rides softer than a mid-point flex might imply. CONSTRUCTION & MATERIALS 93. Core material: FSC™ Certified Super Fly II™ 700G [36] [MERCHANT] 94. Core description: Dual-species wood core; stronger and lighter woods targeted in specific areas for pop, strength, and reduced weight [36] 95. Core profiling: Squeezebox – thicker, more powerful core sections balanced with thinner, more flexible sections [38] 97. Core edge technology: Dualzone™ EGD™ – wood grain positioned along toe and heel edges in two continuous zones, perpendicular to rest of core for consistent edge-hold and strength [39] [MERCHANT] 98. Laminate: 45° Carbon Highlights – full tip-to-tail carbon layer to reduce weight and fine-tune torsional flex [40] [MERCHANT] 99. Laminate fibre angle detail: A 45° fiber angle provides a more aggressive ride feel (vs. 60° which is more playful) [41] 100. Fiberglass type (2022 non-split per Whitelines review): Triax fiberglass weave [43] 102. Base material: Sintered WFO – extra absorbent high-density sintered material infused with specially formulated wax [44] [MERCHANT] 103. Base description (Blauer Board Shop): "Ultra-durable base that stays wide open all season and in any condition" [44] 104. Resin: Super Sap® Epoxy – bio-based materials reducing carbon footprint by 50% over conventional petroleum-based epoxies [45] 105. Mounting system: The Split Channel™ – pre-mounted pucks for easy setup [46] [MERCHANT] 106. Binding compatibility: Compatible with all major bindings (not just Burton's) via Channel system [47] 107. Durability technology: Infinite Ride™ – board is overbuilt then machine-broken-in for consistent flex, pop, and feel from day one [48] [MERCHANT] 108. Construction layers (Zombie Board Shop): 1-Topsheet, 2-Top Glass (0°/UDG & ±45° stitched), 3-Core, 4-Bottom Glass (0°/Carbon & ±45° stitched), 5-Base [49] 109. Forestry certification: FSC™ Certified core wood [36] 110. Sustainability: Super Sap® Epoxy reduces carbon footprint by 50% [45] TERRAIN & RATINGS 111. Park rating: 2/10 [MERCHANT] 112. All mountain rating: 4/10 [MERCHANT] 113. Powder rating: 10/10 [MERCHANT] 114. Rider level (merchant): Intermediate [MERCHANT] 115. Rider level (evo.com): Advanced-Expert [50] 116. Rider level (Backcountry.com): "Expert Powder and Backcountry Riders" [51] DISAGREEMENT: Rider level. The merchant lists "Intermediate," while evo.com classifies it as "Advanced-Expert" and Backcountry.com says "Expert." The board is powder-specific with specialized design features, suggesting it is best suited for experienced riders, though its forgiving flex makes it accessible. 117. Terrain suitability: Backcountry, deep snow, trees [MERCHANT] 118. Terrain focus (Backcountry.com): "Storm days, tight tree runs, and big mountain powder lines" [51] 119. Riding style: Surfy feeling [MERCHANT] 120. Ride characteristic (The Inertia review): "It really felt surfy in the best possible way" [52] 121. Use case: Quiver powder board / dedicated deep day board – not an all-rounder [53] WARRANTY 122. Warranty: 3-year warranty from date of purchase for all 2014+ Burton snowboards with The Channel mounting system [54] 123. Warranty coverage: Against manufacturer's defects; repair or replace at Burton's discretion [55] 124. Warranty limitation: Valid only for original purchaser with proof of purchase from authorized retailer [55] 125. Warranty repair turnaround: Typically 3-4 weeks [56] PERFORMANCE — POSITIVES (FROM REVIEWS) 126. Powder float: Exceptional – "Unsinkable" per Backcountry Magazine tester; "even in waist high pow it didn't feel like the Fish was having trouble staying afloat" (TheGoodRide) [35][57] 127. Tree riding: "This is my favorite board for jamming through trees" (TheGoodRide); "perfect for the tight trees" (Backcountry Magazine) [58][35] 128. Turning: "Super quick. It just went wherever I wanted it to go" (TheGoodRide) [59] 129. Taper feel: "Pretty tapered and directional but it doesn't feel like 30mm of taper. Burton does cool things with the sidecut" (TheGoodRide) [60] 130. Edge-to-edge transitions in powder: Smooth and fun due to 3D tech and lifted sides [61] 131. Ease of buttering: Board butters really easy, likely due to rocker in nose/tail [62] 132. Maneuverability: "There's a maneuverability to this board that is unique in the industry" (The Inertia) [63] 133. Pop: "Good but not exceptional pop on an ollie" (TheGoodRide) [64] 134. Base speed out of box: "Exceptional out of the box" (TheGoodRide) [65] 135. Pre-mounted pucks: Comes with binding pucks ready to go – "really underrated feature" (The Inertia) [66] 136. Swallowtail control: "You can stick that swallow tail anywhere, and it just feels so good" (The Inertia) [67] 137. Award: Backcountry Magazine 2026 Editors' Choice splitboard [35] 138. Heli-skiing popularity: "The world's largest heli operator in BC stocks and rents more Fish – now the 3D Fish – than everything else put together" (snowboarding forum user, former BC heli operator) [68] 139. Topsheet aesthetics: "A gorgeous board with a beautiful top sheet" (The Inertia) [69] 140. Reviewer retention (TheGoodRide): "I planned on selling it after but now its in my quiver" [70] PERFORMANCE — NEGATIVES (FROM REVIEWS) 141. Hard snow / ice performance: "Not at home in steep, hard conditions. The nose feels a tad catchy when the rider has to maneuver in firm snow" (The Inertia) [71] 142. Groomer performance: "Not more than a 4/10 on groomers" (forum user); "doable but far from ideal" (TheGoodRide) [72][73] 143. Icy / windblown conditions: "3D makes it completely useless in windblown or icy crust" (forum user) [74] 144. Base maintenance issue: "Base can get chalky and needs lots of maintenance" after first wax; also occurred with other 2021 Burton boards [75] 145. Pop assessment (forum): "Has no pop" (one forum opinion, compared to review stating "good but not exceptional") [74] 146. Not for bombing/speed riding: "Isn't about bombing but more for those that like to turn. Isn't for powering over chopped up snow or bumps" (TheGoodRide) [76] 147. Skins requirement: Works best with Burton proprietary skins due to swallowtail shape; "I would probably recommend buying the Burton skins with the 3D" (The Inertia) [77] 148. Additional gear required: Splitboarding requires climbing skins, special bindings, and backcountry safety knowledge/equipment [78] 149. Open powder limitation (forum): "For open pow it'd probably be a let down compared to wider boards with more float under foot" (forum user) [79] BOOT SIZE RECOMMENDATIONS (TheGoodRide) 150. Recommended boot size 152cm: US 8-9 [80] 151. Recommended boot size 156cm: US 9-10 [80] 152. Recommended boot size 160/161cm: US 9.5-10.5 [80] 153. Maximum boot size recommendation: Narrower tail is best for keeping it under size 11 (US) [81] COMPARABLE PRODUCTS & ALTERNATIVES 154. Competitor: Jones Storm Chaser (Splitboard) – surf-style powder rocket, designed by Chris Christenson; stiffer flex (7/10), Surf Rocker profile, 3D Contour Base [82] 155. Competitor: Weston Japow – pow-specific slayer; Burton 3D Fish reviewer says "3D Fish is a bit more versatile" [83] 156. Competitor: Lib Tech Escalator Split – "even more versatile board that still rides wide" (The Inertia) [84] 157. Related Burton model (non-split): Burton Fish 3D Directional Flat Top Snowboard (solid, non-split version) [85] 158. Related Burton model: Burton Hometown Hero – camber-based all-mountain/powder hybrid; "Most people who ride both HH and Fish prefer the Fish" for powder (forum) [86] 159. Related Burton model: Burton Pow Wrench – another Burton swallowtail powder board with Fish-derived features [87] 160. Predecessor model: Burton Fish (non-3D) – earlier camber/S-Rocker version with Carbon I-Beam stringer; now out of production in split form [88] 161. 3D Fish vs non-3D Fish (forum): "3D Fish is a bit more stable than the non 3D in the new shape, but with less pop" [89] RIDER SIZE REFERENCE (The Inertia review) 162. Reviewer stats (The Inertia): 6'0", 200 lbs, rode the 156cm – "felt really good, even though it's probably a tad shorter than what I normally ride" [90] 163. Reviewer stats (TheGoodRide): Size 9 boot, 5'10", 185-190 lbs, rode 156cm [91] 164. Volume shift sizing: "The extra width in the nose and mid-section of the board makes up for any lack of length" (The Inertia) [92] ADDITIONAL FEATURES & NOTES 165. 3D base technology detail: Convex shaping in tip and tail with traditional flat base through middle blends edge control and surfy freedom for catch-free tip and tail [93] 166. Setback style: Substantial directional setback; measured reference-to-tail 440mm, reference-to-nose 570mm = 130mm of actual board setback at 161cm [94] 167. Flex direction: Directional flex – increased pop in the tail and more resilient nose [95] 168. Binding recommendation (The Inertia): Burton Step On® Splitboard Binding — reviewer's favorite for touring [96]
